We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with at least 5 reactions, using templates in order: ['29646', '1914389', '1914390', '149040', '1914391'].

We have applied first template 29646 to target, got three possible precursors (three branches). Need to choose one that can be further processed with next template 1914389, then 1914390, then 149040, then 1914391.

We need to construct a tree where each reaction node has children precursors (molecules). The route must be linear? At least 5 reactions, using those templates in order. Likely each step reduces complexity.

We need to find a sequence where each template matches the product of previous step.

We have candidate from first step: three possible products (precursors). Choose one that matches template 1914389.

We tested first candidate: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" matches 1914389 (True). Good.

Second candidate: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO" did not match.

Third candidate: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)[C@H]1C)CO" also not tested but likely not.

Thus we will select first precursor as product of step1.

Now apply template 1914389 to that precursor, we got two products: a tuple of two SMILES? The result: "(('C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C', 'CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC'),)". So applying template yields two fragments: first is a molecule (maybe product after transformation) and second is another fragment (maybe leaving group). For retrosynthesis, we need precursors (reactants) that combine to give the target. So after applying template 1914389, we get two precursors: A = "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](CC=O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C" and B = "CCOC(=O)/C=C/CP(=O)(OCC)OCC". Good.

Now next template 1914390 must be applied to one of these molecules (likely the first) to further break down. We tried matching 1914390 to first molecule and got False. Maybe apply to second? Check.
